{"dimension":"Primary nuisance: yard/blight condition vs vehicle parking location on unpaved/grass","gt_signal":"Complaint centers on yard blight—trash/litter/junk or overgrowth on private property (e.g., 'trash on the lawn', 'toys, litter, candy wrappers')—even if vehicles are mentioned","pr_signal":"Complaint centers on vehicles being stored/parked on grass/yard/unpaved areas or related ticket/paving issues, without a blight/overgrowth/trash focus","culprit":"The PR positive trigger for 'vehicles parked on grass/yard/on the lawn' matched phrases like 'cars parked on the lawn', overruling co-occurring blight terms","fix":"Prioritize yard blight indicators (trash/litter/overgrowth) over vehicle-on-lawn cues when both appear; only use Parking on Unimproved Surface when the report is primarily about vehicles on grass/unpaved or parking/ticket/paving issues."}

{"dimension":"Source/object of the hazard: yard blight (vegetation/junk on the grounds) vs the building’s structural integrity/security","gt_signal":"Issues confined to the yard or exterior grounds—overgrown grass/weeds or junk/debris/appliances on the property—without a specific structural defect or unsecured building","pr_signal":"Explicit risk tied to a structure being unsafe or unsealed—vacant/unsecured buildings, broken windows, collapsing/falling structures, holes in foundation, long-standing unsafe scaffolding, unsafe outbuildings","culprit":"Over-broad triggering on 'unsecured'/'unsafe' in the Unsafe Buildings rule, matching an unsecured refrigerator and a vague 'house appears unsafe' without structural evidence","fix":"Constrain Unsafe Buildings to conditions naming a building/outbuilding’s structural or security failure, and send yard appliances/junk or overgrowth to Excessive Growth even if described as 'unsafe' or 'unsecured'."}

{"pos":["Missed or partial household trash pickup: missed/not picked up, return requested, no notice left, or neighbors collected but not here.","Trash service compliance: pay‑per‑bag stickers required, cart/can exceeds size or weight limits, unacceptable trash containers, or improper set‑out/placement.","Refuse/debris removal: dumped garbage, bulky items (couch/mattress/desk), overflowing dumpsters/carts, or waste causing odors/rodents/animal scattering.","Hauler handling issues: trash bag ripped/dragged, spillage, or carts placed improperly by crew.","Bulky household item at curb awaiting trash pickup for days/weeks."],"remap":["if explicit yard‑waste stream (yard waste/brush/leaves) or its rules (40‑lb limit, seasonal suspension, yard‑waste stickers/fees, plastic‑bag ban), classify as Yard Waste instead","if complaint is about recycling/recyclables, including missed/not picked up or sorting/contamination (e.g., no bags, please sort), classify as Recycling instead","if trash/junk is accumulating on private property (yard/side/behind/parking lot/alley) with no curbside/hauler/dumpster context, classify as Excessive Growth instead","if the concern is obstruction of travel/right‑of‑way without overflow/dumped‑waste cleanup intent, classify as Blocked Street instead"]}

{"pos":["Explicit yard‑waste/brush/leaves/branches term or 40‑lb limit, with set‑out compliance: required sticker/fee, 35‑gal can oversize/overfilled, or overweight.","Yard‑waste referenced container/prep violation: in plastic bags, improper container, not tied/bundled brush, packed too tight, or prohibited contents like dirt/rocks.","Yard‑waste program timing/season rules: not out by required time, wrong day, no winter collection, seasonal suspension, or placement violations.","Contamination involving yard waste: garbage mixed with yard waste or non‑program items included with brush/leaves.","Courtesy pickup documented for a yard‑waste violation/education, with explicit yard‑waste/brush/leaves reference."],"remap":["if sticker or 35‑gal/can size compliance is noted without any yard‑waste/brush/leaves/branches terms, classify as Trash instead","if complaint is a missed pickup/collection, even when yard‑waste is mentioned, classify as Trash instead","if recycling, recycle/blue cart/bin, or recyclables (bottles, cans, paper) are referenced, classify as Recycling instead","if tie/bundle requirement concerns cardboard or boxes without yard‑waste terms, classify as Recycling instead"]}

{"pos":["Overgrown vegetation on private property: tall grass/weeds/shrubs/hedges, including vacant lots and neglected yards","Private-property overgrowth encroaching onto sidewalks, driveways, or corner views from a specific yard, hedge, or fence","Accumulation of non-garbage junk/debris or scattered litter on private grounds, porches, alleys, or parking lots, absent curbside service context","Property-generated yard waste, limbs, or residents’ containers/debris creating a cleanup issue, even when spilling into adjacent sidewalk/right‑of‑way"],"remap":["if household garbage, dumpster overflow, dumped bulky item (couch/mattress/appliance), or odor/rodents are mentioned, classify as Trash instead","if vegetation in the public right‑of‑way or city‑maintained area creates a traffic sightline hazard, classify as Line of Sight instead","if a freestanding object placed in the street/sidewalk (e.g., roll‑off dumpster/equipment) is the obstruction, classify as Blocked Street instead","if rocks/gravel/backfill or yard/drive damage after water utility digs, meter/line work, or restoration requests, classify as Water Utility Problems instead"]}

{"pos":["Explicit recycling cue (recycling/recyclables/blue cart/bin) plus unsorted, mixed with trash/non-program items, or contamination noted.","Explicit recycling cue plus instruction or violation about preparation: please sort, no bags, rinse/empty, flatten or bundle cardboard.","Non-recyclable items placed in a recycling cart/bin or recyclables placed in plastic bags or outside required container.","Crew note or tag citing contaminated recycling (food, feces, cigarette butts) requiring education/compliance.","Items set out as recycling are not included in the recycling program."],"remap":["if collection failure is described (missed, not picked up, please pick up, no notice, others collected but not here), classify as Trash instead","if text references yard waste stream (yard waste, brush, leaves, grass, clippings), classify as Yard Waste instead","if contamination framed as garbage mixed with yard waste, classify as Yard Waste instead","if yard-waste-specific set-out is the issue (bundling limbs/brush, yard waste in plastic bags, sticker or weight limit), classify as Yard Waste instead"]}

{"pos":["Vegetation within the public right-of-way, shoulder, ditch, or median blocks motorists’ view at an intersection, corner, or driveway onto a public roadway.","Vegetation within a traffic island, roundabout, or median blocks drivers’ view of entering or circulating vehicles.","Risk Management reports a traffic visibility “line of sight” vegetation hazard on a public street.","Roadside vegetation in the public right-of-way reduces sight distance around a curve or hill on a public road.","Vegetation encroaching from a city-owned parcel abutting a street limits drivers’ ability to see cross-traffic when entering or crossing the roadway."],"remap":["if overgrowth originates from a specific private property’s hedge, fence, or yard (named address/parcel), even at a corner, classify as Excessive Growth instead","if the issue is a sidewalk or path overgrown/impassable, forcing pedestrians into the street, classify as Excessive Growth instead","if the request is trimming a private frontage for aesthetics/property upkeep, not motorists’ visibility on a public road, classify as Excessive Growth instead","if sightlines are blocked by non-vegetation objects (parked vehicles, dumpsters, construction equipment or materials), classify as Blocked Street instead"]}

{"pos":["Reports of clogged/blocked storm drains, inlets, catch basins, driveway culverts, or ditches.","Storm sewer backing up, surcharging, or not conveying runoff during/after rain.","Standing or ponded water on streets or public right-of-way from poor drainage or blocked inlets.","Flooding of properties or businesses attributed to rainfall, runoff, grading, or development drainage changes.","Requests to install, adjust, or maintain public drainage components (standpipes, culverts, inlets, pipes, outfalls)."],"remap":["if references water mains/service lines, meters, valves, hydrants, or shutoffs, classify as Water Utility Problems instead.","if yard-only standing water with no rain/storm/drain terms and suspected leak, classify as Water Utility Problems instead.","if sanitary sewer backups, manholes overflowing, or sewage odors, classify as Sewer Problems instead.","if snow or ice on sidewalks or failure to shovel sidewalks, classify as Street Snow Removal instead."]}

{"pos":["Explicit failures or leaks of public water distribution assets: mains/service lines, hydrants, curb-stop/shutoff valves, or meters/meter pits/lids.","Standing water or saturated ground on private yard/property suspected from underground water-line leak, not linked to rainfall or drainage infrastructure.","Reports of dirty/sooty/gritty water or persistent discoloration affecting whole residence/units, indicating system flushing/repair needed beyond a single tap.","Restoration complaints following water utility excavations: rocks/backfill left, settlement, or requests to repair yards/driveways disturbed by water-line work.","Field operations at curb stop expressly for repairs (e.g., shutoff/turn-on for plumber or leak repair), not for account activation/deactivation."],"remap":["if standing water references rain, storm drains/inlets/culverts/ditches/standpipes, street ponding/flooding, or grading/runoff, classify as Sidewalk Snow Removal instead.","if request is to start/stop service or turn water on/off without a break/leak/fault, classify as Water Quality instead.","if issue is taste, odor, color, pressure, or noise at taps/appliances with no explicit public-asset failure, classify as Water Quality instead.","if complaint involves sanitary sewer performance, sewer manholes, backups/slow flushing, dye/connection tests, classify as Sewer Problems (Sanitary Sewers) instead."]}

{"pos":["Intentionally placed freestanding objects or equipment (dumpsters, trailers, storage pods) occupying street, alley, sidewalk, or tree lawn and blocking passage.","Construction materials or machinery staged in the public right‑of‑way that impede movement, absent any sanitation or trash‑overflow concern.","Private items placed in the tree plot/tree lawn that obstruct curb, sidewalk, or access, beyond momentary loading/unloading.","Long‑term placement of roll‑off dumpsters or storage containers on a street or alley without active loading, reducing lane width or access."],"remap":["if bushes, weeds, or trees from a specific property encroach onto sidewalk or right‑of‑way, classify as Excessive Growth instead","if complaint centers on dumpster overflow, scattered garbage, odor, or a request for pickup/cleanup, classify as Trash instead","if residents’ trash or recycling carts are left or rolling in the street or blocking the sidewalk, classify as Trash instead","if bulky items, brush piles, or dumped debris are left at curb, street, or alley for removal, classify as Trash instead"]}

{"pos":["Tap-side sensory complaints: unusual taste/odor or non-dirty color (e.g., blue), with no debris and no prolonged discoloration reported","In-home plumbing symptoms: low pressure, sputtering/air, or pipe banging/rattling; or a request to check pressure at the customer meter","Requests to start, stop, turn on/off water service or account activation, without citing an outage or field valve/curb-stop operation","Customer seeks help with in-home water appliances (heater, softener, filter) or plumbing fixtures, not reporting utility-owned equipment failure","Reports of a leak at or near the residence with no explicit main, meter box/pit, curb stop, or street/right-of-way mentioned"],"remap":["if water is described as dirty/discolored with particles (e.g., black sooty) or lasting days/weeks, classify as Water Utility Problems instead","if a leak is explicitly at a main, meter box/pit, curb stop, fire hydrant, or street/road/right-of-way, or contractor-damaged valve, classify as Water Utility Problems instead","if request explicitly mentions curb-stop/curb valve operation, utility shutoff/turn-on at street, or meter pull/install, classify as Water Utility Problems instead","if issue affects multiple units/building or multiple homes/neighborhood, or has onsite maintenance for building-wide water, classify as Water Utility Problems instead"]}

{"pos":["Vacant/abandoned building with broken/missing doors/windows or unsealed openings permitting entry or weather intrusion.","Visible structural failure or imminent collapse of a building or accessory structure: leaning, partial collapse, holes in foundation/roof, separating from chimney.","Detached garage, shed, or outbuilding reported unsafe, collapsing, or needing boarding/sealing to prevent entry.","Scaffolding or temporary shoring left long-term or visibly unstable, posing collapse or falling-debris risk to the public.","Fire-damaged structure reported unsecured or structurally unsafe following a fire incident report."],"remap":["if overgrown vegetation, yard junk, or appliances on the property are the issue without a specific building defect/unsecured opening, classify as Excessive Growth instead","if stored hazardous materials or construction debris (e.g., gasoline, asbestos insulation) on porch/yard are the hazard, classify as Trash instead","if the request cites permits, inspections, or prior notices rather than a physical hazard, classify as Trash instead","if an occupied dwelling reports only maintenance defects (e.g., broken windows, rickety stairs) without vacancy, unsecured access, or collapse risk, classify as Trash instead"]}

{"pos":["Vehicle(s) parked on grass, dirt, or other unpaved areas of private residential or commercial property (front, side, or rear yards).","Oversized vehicles—RVs, boats, trailers, or commercial trucks—parked on lawns or other unimproved surfaces of private lots.","Repeated or ongoing use of yard/unpaved surface for parking or vehicle storage, regardless of available driveway space.","Requests seeking enforcement of code/ordinance prohibiting parking on grass/unimproved surfaces of private property.","Administrative matters explicitly about this violation: citation or notice for parking on grass/unimproved surface, hearing, permit, or fine."],"remap":["if vehicles are described as inoperable/abandoned or kept for months on the property, classify as Trash instead","if the complaint centers on junk, debris, or auto parts (e.g., tires) accumulated on the property, classify as Trash instead","if yard conditions—litter, toys, candy wrappers, or overgrowth—are the primary nuisance mentioned, classify as Excessive Growth instead","if report is about blocking a street, alley, driveway, or sidewalk in the public right-of-way, classify as Blocked Street instead"]}

{"pos":["Sewage backing up, toilets or drains slow/gurgling, or wastewater not leaving a building or sewer lateral","Sewer odors/gas (rotten egg/sulfur) in structures or outdoors near drains, cleanouts, or sewer lines","Sewage overflowing, pooling, or leaking onto streets, yards, or waterways; sanitary lift-station or sewage pump alarms/failures causing discharge","Manhole cover missing/loose or manhole defect, when identified as a sewer manhole or generic 'manhole' in roadway/sidewalk","Requests for sewer dye tests or to verify sanitary sewer connection, lateral location, or sewer tap status"],"remap":["if report mentions water main/valve/meter/hydrant, water pressure/quality, or potable service-line leak, classify as Water Utility Problems instead","if storm drain/catch basin/culvert/ditch or rain-runoff flooding is described, classify as Storm Drainage Problems instead","if odor/leak concerns natural gas, appliances, furnace, or water heater with no sewer/drain mention, classify as Gas Utility Problems instead","if taste/odor complaint is about tap water from faucets, classify as Water Utility Problems instead"]}

{"dimension":"Which service stream’s rules are being enforced (yard‑waste program vs household trash), not the type of violation (sticker/size/weight/missed pickup).","gt_signal":"The text anchors the yard‑waste stream—explicit yard‑waste/brush/leaves mention or a yard‑waste‑specific constraint/fee (notably the 40‑lb limit or a “yardwaste” sticker), including when saying a pickup was missed.","pr_signal":"Only generic compliance cues with no stream context (sticker required, can >35 gal, exceeds weight) or stock “bags must have sticker attached” phrasing that implies pay‑per‑bag trash.","culprit":"Overbroad Trash “service compliance” rule that fires on sticker/size/weight regardless of stream, plus a Yard Waste neg that routes missed yard‑waste pickups to Trash.","fix":"Treat compliance and missed‑pickup notes as stream‑specific: if the text names yard waste or uses a yard‑waste‑only threshold/fee (e.g., 40‑lb limit or yard‑waste sticker), keep it in Yard Waste; default to Trash only when no yard‑waste signal exists."}

{"dimension":"What is being abated: sanitary refuse removal (garbage/litter/bulky refuse) vs property maintenance blight (vegetation/neglect/non‑garbage clutter)","gt_signal":"Explicit garbage/refuse as the cleanup target—bags of trash, litter, dumped garbage, overflowing/loose trash, or bulky household items—requesting removal, regardless of being on private property","pr_signal":"Vegetation neglect (grass/weeds/hedges) or a general blight/“yard is a mess” framing on private property without a clear discrete refuse/removal focus","culprit":"Trash.neg rule “if trash/junk is accumulating on private property… classify as Excessive Growth” and Excessive Growth.pos “scattered litter on private grounds… absent curbside context”","fix":"Do not use location (private yard) as the divider; classify any garbage/litter/bags/bulky refuse as Trash, reserving Excessive Growth for vegetation overgrowth or non‑garbage property neglect."}

{"dimension":"Responsibility/intent: private-property nuisance (code enforcement) vs municipal trash collection/cleanup service","gt_signal":"Accumulation or litter on/around a specific property (rear/side yard, between houses, on lawn, behind/around a business/parking lot) or a property compliance issue (e.g., missing dumpster gate), with no curbside/hauler/collection context—even if it mentions bags, a dumpster, or rodents","pr_signal":"References to pickup/hauler logistics (curbside setouts, stickers, cart/dumpster service or overflow), illegal dumping in public right‑of‑way, odors/rodents tied to serviced containers, or an explicit request for city removal","culprit":"Excessive Growth neg rule that auto-routes any mention of household garbage/odors/rodents/dumpster to Trash, overriding the private‑property context","fix":"Prioritize location and responsibility: if waste/litter is stored or accumulating on private property or is a property compliance issue, classify as Excessive Growth regardless of words like trash, bags, dumpster, or rodents; reserve Trash for curb/hauler service problems, serviced-container overflow, or dumping in the right‑of‑way."}

{"dimension":"Waste stream/program context: is the notice enforcing the general household trash stream or the yard‑waste program, not the numeric limits themselves","gt_signal":"No explicit yard‑waste material/program terms; only generic compliance cues like stickers required, 35/32‑gal can or 40‑lb overweight, and non‑vegetative contents like dirt/concrete without a yard‑waste reference","pr_signal":"Explicit yard‑waste stream/material or program cues (yard waste/brush/leaves/branches/Christmas tree, bundling/no‑plastic‑bags, winter suspension), sometimes alongside the same 40‑lb/35‑gal limits","culprit":"Yard Waste positive rule treating '40‑lb limit/35‑gal can' and 'prohibited contents like dirt/rocks' as yard‑waste signals even without an explicit yard‑waste term","fix":"Require an explicit yard‑waste material/program cue to classify as Yard Waste; otherwise treat bare weight/size/sticker/composition violations (even mentioning 40‑lb/35‑gal or dirt/concrete) as Trash."}

{"dimension":"problem type: collection failure (service outcome) vs recycling prep/contamination (compliance)","gt_signal":"language of a failed pickup event—missed/not picked up, no notice, others collected but not here, return requested—even when the stream mentioned is recycling","pr_signal":"recycling-specific compliance cues—unsorted/not properly sorted, contamination, no bags, rinse/flatten, program-ineligible items—without a missed-pickup/collection-failure request","culprit":"Trash.neg: 'if complaint is about recycling/recyclables, including missed/not picked up ... classify as Recycling instead' (conflicts with Recycling.neg and overrides the collection-failure signal)","fix":"Treat any report whose core issue is a missed/failed pickup as Trash regardless of stream; reserve Recycling for preparation/contamination education when no collection-failure is being reported."}

{"dimension":"Service stream being discussed (recycling vs trash), not the operational issue type (missed/compliance)","gt_signal":"Any cue that the issue is about the recycling stream (recycling/recyclables/blue cart/bin, sorted properly, recycling route/crew, courtesy pickup for recycling, container-size or set‑out compliance for the recycling cart)","pr_signal":"Generic missed‑pickup/compliance language with no stream specified, or phrases the rules tie to trash (e.g., can exceeds size limit, stickers) causing default to the trash stream","culprit":"Recycling neg rule: 'if collection failure is described (missed, not picked up, please pick up, no notice, others collected but not here), classify as Trash instead'","fix":"Decide by stream first: if the text indicates the recycling stream, keep it in Recycling even when it’s a miss/courtesy pickup or container/set‑out compliance; only trash‑stream misses belong in Trash."}

{"dimension":"Cause/source and infrastructure domain of the water: storm/runoff drainage vs failures in the pressurized potable water system","gt_signal":"Water tied to rain/runoff, drainage/grade or development changes; street ponding/flooding; erosion; mentions of storm sewers/inlets/culverts/standpipes/outfalls; requests to install/adjust drainage components","pr_signal":"Explicit potable-water assets or operations named (main, service line, meter/pit/lid, hydrant, curb stop/shutoff), “main break,” dirty water at taps, or unexplained yard saturation with no rain/drainage/street/storm‑drain terms","culprit":"An over-broad Water Utility trigger on generic “standing water,” “yard,” or “pipe” terms that ignored rain/drainage/street/storm-pipe cues","fix":"Differentiate by cause: anything linked to rain/runoff, street ponding, erosion, or storm‑drain components goes to stormwater, while Water Utility requires explicit potable-asset terms or clear leak suspicion without rain/drainage language"}

{"dimension":"Which underground utility system is implicated: sanitary sewer conveyance vs. potable water distribution.","gt_signal":"Explicit sewer-side assets or behaviors: mentions of sewer/manhole, dye/connection tests, sewer pump/lift issues discharging to street, sluggish/slow sewer flushing, clogs/backups, requests to check city sewer lines, or restoration explicitly after a sewer main project.","pr_signal":"Explicit potable-water distribution assets or system effects: mains/services/hydrants/curb-stops/meters/pits/lids, main breaks or damaged shutoffs, whole‑unit dirty/sooty water, saturated yard suspected from a water‑line leak, or restoration tied to water‑line work.","culprit":"Water Utility positive cues were too asset-agnostic—‘restoration after utility excavations’ and ‘meter lids’ matched generic ‘restoration’/‘cover’ even when the text named sewer assets (sewer main, manhole), and phrases like ‘water running down street’ were treated as water-line leaks despite a stated sewer pump source.","fix":"Only classify as Water Utility Problems when a potable-water asset or distribution-system effect is explicitly indicated; if sewer-specific assets/diagnostics (sewer, manhole, dye test, sewer pump, slow/backed-up sewer) are named, keep it in Sewer Problems regardless of generic words like water, cover, or restoration."}

{"dimension":"traffic-safety sight distance vs private-property maintenance/encroachment","gt_signal":"driver visibility is impaired at an intersection/corner/driveway/curve (e.g., “can’t see to pull out,” “line of sight,” named road corners, Risk Management visibility report) with focus on motorists and roadway safety","pr_signal":"the issue is the condition or encroachment of vegetation/junk on a specific property (tall grass, weeds, yard/hedge overgrowth, sidewalk/yard impacts) without a motorist visibility context","culprit":"the Line of Sight negative rule that forces anything originating from a specific private property’s hedge/fence/yard—even at a corner—into Excessive Growth","fix":"Treat any vegetation that impairs motorists’ sight distance on public roads (intersections, corners, driveways, curves, medians) as Line of Sight regardless of property ownership, and reserve Excessive Growth for private overgrowth not affecting drivers’ visibility."}

{"dimension":"Source/ownership of the obstructing vegetation (private parcel vs public right‑of‑way/city‑maintained)","gt_signal":"Cues that the growth originates from a specific private property—mentions of a yard, hedge, fence line, driveway, corner lot/cul‑de‑sac—i.e., encroachment from a parcel onto the public way","pr_signal":"Vegetation clearly in the public right‑of‑way/median/city parcel or tied to roadway infrastructure (e.g., stop sign, arterial/avenue, traffic island) causing motorists’ visibility hazards, with no indicators it’s a private yard/hedge","culprit":"Intersection/visibility phrasing (\"intersection\", \"can’t see\", \"dangerous\") is over-weighted to Line of Sight, while the model ignores private-origin cues like \"yard/hedge/driveway/corner\" and seems to require a named address to treat it as private","fix":"Prioritize origin: treat reports implying a specific yard/hedge/driveway/corner lot as Excessive Growth even when they mention visibility at an intersection, and reserve Line of Sight for vegetation in the public right‑of‑way/medians/city property or tied to traffic control devices."}

{"dimension":"Intent/stage of work: customer-service/diagnostic at tap/meter vs confirmed utility-asset repair","gt_signal":"Non-fault requests or diagnostics: account turn-on/turn-off, tap-level symptoms, or meter-side checks, including vague/unconfirmed 'leak' reports without evidence of a broken public asset or standing water","pr_signal":"Explicit infrastructure failure/repair context: main/service-line breaks, standing water/saturated ground, damaged meters/meter pits/lids/valves, contractor damage, or system-wide dirty/sooty water; shutoff/turn-on only when tied to a repair/plumber","culprit":"Overbroad Water Utility Problems positives for 'shutoff/turn-on' and 'leaks at meters/meter pits' (and the keyword 'leak') that fired without any repair/failure context","fix":"Require explicit evidence of a public-asset failure or repair context for Water Utility Problems; otherwise, treat account start/stop and meter/tap inspections or unconfirmed leaks as Water Quality."}

{"dimension":"Imminent structural/public-entry hazard vs. routine/occupied maintenance or administrative issues","gt_signal":"Reports mention occupancy or only minor defects/admin matters (broken windows, wobbly stairs, permits/inspections) with no vacancy, unsecured entry, fire damage, or visible structural failure.","pr_signal":"Explicit vacancy/abandonment, unsealed openings permitting entry, fire-damaged/unsecured structures, visible structural failure/collapse risk, or long‑term unstable scaffolding/outbuildings.","culprit":"Keyword bias toward “broken windows,” “unsafe,” and “building” triggered Unsafe Buildings without checking for vacancy/unsecured access or actual structural failure.","fix":"Gate Unsafe Buildings on clear vacancy/unsecured access or structural failure; if occupied or only maintenance/permit concerns are described, route to Trash."}

{"dimension":"Which material stream the note is evaluating (yard‑waste set‑out vs recycling set‑out), not which contaminant is named","gt_signal":"The subject is the yard‑waste stream: violations or prep instructions about brush/leaves set‑out (bundling, containers, weight/season/timing) or contamination of a yard‑waste pile/cart with non‑program items—even if those contaminants are recyclables like cardboard","pr_signal":"The subject is the recycling stream: issues about preparing or sorting recyclables, recycling cart/bin contamination, or bundling/flattening cardboard for recycling, typically keyed to a recycling container or explicit recycling prep context","culprit":"Over‑reliance on surface cues: Recycling pos rule (explicit 'recycling' + contamination) and Yard‑Waste neg rule (tie/bundle about cardboard -> Recycling)","fix":"Classify by the stream being inspected—keep contamination or prep notes with the yard‑waste set‑out in Yard Waste even if they mention recyclables/cardboard, and require a recycling‑container/context anchor to assign Recycling."}

{"dimension":"Intent/responsibility: utility restoration of disturbed ground/drive vs private vegetation/yard maintenance/cleanup","gt_signal":"Requests to restore or repair yards/driveways (e.g., drive repair, yard restoration, backfill/settlement, post-dig cleanup) or mention of water-utility assets/repairs","pr_signal":"Conditions of vegetation or property neglect—tall grass/weeds, needs mowing, overgrown shrubs, junk/litter—without any repair/restoration intent","culprit":"The keyword “yard/yard work” was treated as an Excessive Growth cue instead of recognizing it as a yard/drive restoration request","fix":"Treat yard/drive restoration or repair (e.g., “yard work,” “drive repair,” backfill/settlement, post-dig restoration) as Water Utility Problems, and reserve Excessive Growth for vegetation/junk conditions like tall grass, weeds, or litter."}

{"dimension":"Placement surface of a vehicle vs obstruction of the public right‑of‑way by non‑vehicle objects","gt_signal":"Mentions a vehicle on grass/dirt/yard or other unpaved ground (even partially, e.g., at a path/greenspace entrance), with focus on the unimproved surface rather than blockage","pr_signal":"Mentions dumpsters/containers/equipment or similar items staged in the street/alley/sidewalk/tree lawn that impede passage—longer‑term objects in the right‑of‑way, not cars","culprit":"Lexical cues like “street”/“path opening” steered to Blocked Street, compounded by Parking-on‑Unimproved rules emphasizing private property and missing vehicles on public greenspace","fix":"Classify any report of a vehicle on grass/unpaved ground—on private yards or public greenspace, even if partly in the street—as Parking on Unimproved Surface, and reserve Blocked Street for non‑vehicle objects obstructing the right‑of‑way."}

{"dimension":"Effect on the public travelway vs. private property maintenance","gt_signal":"It describes vegetation intruding into the public right‑of‑way/roadway (“three feet into the right of way”), i.e., an obstruction that impedes passage in the street/sidewalk/alley regardless of the obstruction’s material.","pr_signal":"Mentions of grass/weeds/shrubbery tied to a specific property and framed as trimming/maintenance (“needs to be trimmed back,” lawn/lot conditions) without explicitly stating the public way is blocked.","culprit":"Blocked Street neg rule: “if bushes, weeds, or trees from a specific property encroach onto sidewalk or right‑of‑way, classify as Excessive Growth instead.”","fix":"Classify any obstruction that encroaches into and impedes movement in the public right‑of‑way as Blocked Street—even if caused by vegetation—reserving Excessive Growth for overgrowth that is a property‑maintenance issue not blocking travel."}

{"pos":["Obstructions or failures in stormwater conveyance: storm drain, inlet, catch basin, culvert, ditch, outfall, standpipe; including storm sewer backing up or not conveying runoff.","Standing or ponded water on streets or public right-of-way, typically after rain or from blocked storm inlets.","Flooding or erosion on properties or businesses explicitly tied to rainfall, runoff, grading, or development drainage changes.","Requests to install, adjust, repair, or maintain public stormwater components: culverts, inlets, pipes, outfalls, standpipes, swales, ditches.","Street or intersection flooding recurring during storms, regardless of nearby private property impacts."],"remap":["if references water mains, service lines, meters, valves, hydrants, or shutoffs, classify as Water Utility Problems instead.","if yard-only standing water or soggy lawn with suspected leak and no rain/runoff/drainage terms, classify as Water Utility Problems instead.","if sanitary sewer backups, manholes overflowing, basement sewage, or sewage odors, classify as Sewer Problems instead.","if snow or ice on sidewalks, unshoveled sidewalks, or sidewalk plowing requests, classify as Street Snow Removal instead."]}

{"pos":["Report of sewage/sewer backup, overflow, clog, or slow drainage implicating sanitary sewers, laterals, mains, or manholes (indoors or discharging to street).","Sewer or rotten-egg/H2S odor complaints indoors or outdoors, including health symptoms attributed to sewer gas.","Requests involving city sanitary sewer assets: inspect/flush/check lines or manholes, or restoration/yard repair explicitly tied to sanitary sewer main/lateral work.","Dye or smoke tests to verify sanitary sewer connections, cross-connections, or service status.","Failures/leaks of sanitary sewer pumps, lift/grinder stations, or private ejector pumps, especially discharging wastewater/sewage to ground or street, or alarmed."],"remap":["if explicit potable-water asset (water main/service line/meter/hydrant/valve) or drinking-water pressure/quality issue, and no sewer-specific asset/diagnostic named, classify as Water Utility Problems instead","if issue concerns storm drain/catch basin/storm sewer or rain-related street flooding, classify as Storm Drain Issues instead","if odor reported is natural gas/fuel/chemical, not sewage/H2S, classify as Gas Utility Problems instead"]}

{"pos":["Vegetation limits motorists’ ability to see cross‑traffic when approaching or entering a public intersection, corner, roundabout, or merge.","Vegetation obstructs drivers’ sight distance when exiting a driveway or alley onto a public roadway.","Vegetation in a median, island, shoulder, ditch, or right‑of‑way reduces sight distance around a curve or hill.","Vegetation blocks motorists’ view of oncoming vehicles or traffic control needed to proceed safely on a public street.","Risk Management or traffic safety staff report a vegetation‑related sight distance hazard on a public road."],"remap":["if the complaint concerns overgrowth impeding sidewalks, paths, or pedestrian travel rather than motorists’ visibility, classify as Excessive Growth instead","if it references a private yard/hedge/fence or a driveway frontage without mentioning entering/crossing a public roadway, classify as Excessive Growth instead","if it reports “overgrown” corners at an intersection without any visibility/line‑of‑sight/sight‑distance wording, classify as Excessive Growth instead","if sightlines are blocked by non‑vegetation (vehicles, dumpsters, equipment, construction materials), classify as Blocked Street instead"]}

{"pos":["Vacant or abandoned building has broken/missing doors/windows or other unsealed openings allowing public entry or weather intrusion.","Any structure shows visible structural failure or imminent collapse: leaning, partial collapse, foundation/roof holes, or separation from chimney or wall.","Detached garage, shed, or outbuilding reported unsafe or collapsing, or requiring boarding/sealing to prevent unauthorized entry.","Fire-damaged building reported unsecured or structurally unsafe after a fire incident.","Scaffolding or temporary shoring left long-term or visibly unstable, posing collapse or falling-debris risk to the public."],"remap":["if the dwelling is stated occupied and only minor defects are reported (e.g., broken window, rickety stairs), classify as Trash instead.","if the complaint references permits, inspection scheduling, or scope compliance without describing a physical hazard, classify as Trash instead.","if the issue is junk, debris, or hazardous materials on the porch/yard rather than a building defect, classify as Trash instead.","if the request concerns people living there or welfare checks without any building defect or unsecured opening, classify as Trash instead."]}

{"dimension":"Service stream/program context (yard organics vs household trash), not the type of infraction","gt_signal":"Explicit yard‑organics context: mentions of yard waste/yardwaste/brush/leaves/branches or yard‑waste program cues (seasonal rules, courtesy tied to yard waste), which should override whether it’s a missed pickup or a sticker/size/weight note","pr_signal":"Issue-only compliance language with no stream cue (missed pickup, stickers required, can exceeds 35 gal, exceeds weight limit), which the current rules default to the generic Trash stream","culprit":"The Yard Waste negative rule that sends any missed pickup to Trash, plus the fallback that routes sticker/35‑gal/weight notes without yard‑waste terms to Trash and failure to recognize the 'yardwaste' variant, all of which overrode true yard‑waste context","fix":"Prioritize stream over issue: if the text indicates the yard‑waste stream (including the 'yardwaste' spelling), keep it in Yard Waste even when it mentions missed pickup or sticker/size/weight/courtesy; only default such generic compliance phrasing to Trash when no yard‑waste context exists."}

{"dimension":"Material‑stream specificity: is the note explicitly about the yard‑waste stream (content/program) or just generic set‑out compliance that applies to any refuse","gt_signal":"Only generic compliance cues (40‑lb/35‑gal limits, sticker requirements) with no yard‑waste material words, or a missed pickup regardless of material","pr_signal":"Explicit yard‑waste identifiers (yard waste/brush/leaves) or yard‑waste‑only prep cues like “no dirt,” “in plastic bags,” or “yardwaste sticker”","culprit":"Yard Waste positive rule that fires on the 40‑lb limit (and similar compliance cues) even without any yard‑waste/brush/leaves terms","fix":"Require an explicit yard‑waste stream indicator (content or YW‑only prep) to classify as Yard Waste; otherwise treat bare weight/size/sticker violations and any missed pickups as Trash."}

{"dimension":"Material type/public-health risk: putrescible household garbage/refuse vs vegetation or inert property clutter (sanitation vs maintenance)","gt_signal":"Mentions of household garbage/refuse (bags of trash, garbage, litter, overflowing/dumped refuse, bulky household items, odors/rodents) even if on private property or in a back/front yard and without curbside context","pr_signal":"Absence of household garbage; instead overgrown grass/weeds or accumulation of non-putrescible junk/clutter on private grounds framed as a yard/property maintenance issue","culprit":"Trash.neg rule that reroutes private‑property trash/junk to Excessive Growth, plus EG.pos phrasing that treats “scattered litter” as Excessive Growth","fix":"Decide by waste type, not location: household garbage/bagged trash/litter or dumped bulky items are Trash even on private property; Excessive Growth is vegetation or inert junk/clutter only."}

{"dimension":"Responsible party / service context: private‑property blight vs collection/hauler service issue","gt_signal":"A condition on private grounds (rear/side yard, on lawn, between houses, around/behind a business or its lot) with no curbside pickup, container, hauler, or sticker/size context—accumulated junk/litter/garbage as a property‑maintenance problem, even if many bags, rats, or a dumpster enclosure are mentioned.","pr_signal":"References to the trash service process, rules, or containers (missed pickup/return, stickers required, can/cart size, curb/alley set‑out, overflowing service dumpsters/carts, crew actions) indicating city/hauler responsibility.","culprit":"The Excessive Growth negative rule that reroutes any mention of household garbage/rodents/dumpster to Trash.","fix":"Route to Trash only when there is collection/hauler context (curbside set‑out, service dumpsters/carts, or hauler actions), and keep any accumulation on private property grounds under Excessive Growth even if it’s bagged household garbage, mentions rats, or refers to a dumpster enclosure."}

{"dimension":"Operational service failure vs. recycling-preparation/compliance","gt_signal":"Mentions a missed or partial pickup and a request/expectation for service (missed, not picked up, no notice, others collected but not here), even if the word 'recycling' appears.","pr_signal":"Focus on how recyclables were set out or whether they meet program rules (unsorted, must be sorted, no bags, contamination, non-program items), with an instructional/violation tone rather than a pickup redo.","culprit":"Trash.neg rule: \"if complaint is about recycling/recyclables, including missed/not picked up ... classify as Recycling instead\"","fix":"Treat all collection-failure/return-service complaints as Trash regardless of stream mention, and reserve Recycling for sorting/contamination/preparation issues only."}

{"dimension":"Collection stream identity (recycling vs trash), not the type of problem (missed pickup, compliance, courtesy pickup)","gt_signal":"Explicit recycling cues (recycling/recyclables/blue cart/bin) or context showing the issue is about the recycling stream—missed/late or courtesy pickups, cart size/placement, or private recycling service","pr_signal":"Generic missed-pickup/compliance phrases (missed, courtesy p.u., can too big) without an explicit recycling cue, or trash-specific compliance terms like stickers, leading to defaulting to Trash","culprit":"Recycling NEG rule that sends any collection failure (missed/not picked up/please pick up) to Trash","fix":"Prioritize stream identity: if the text indicates the recycling stream, keep it in Recycling even for missed/late pickups, courtesy pickups, or container-size/placement; reserve Trash for trash-stream issues only."}

{"dimension":"Causal source/responsible system: stormwater drainage/runoff vs potable-water distribution/leak","gt_signal":"Mentions of rain/runoff/drainage behavior (street ponding, storm drains/inlets/culverts/ditches/standpipes), erosion/upstream/ravine, grading/development impacts, or requests to add/modify drainage features—even when occurring on private property","pr_signal":"Explicit water-utility assets or failures (main/service/hydrant/meter/valve/curb stop), systemwide dirty water, restoration after water-utility digs, or yard saturation attributed to an underground service leak with no rain/drainage context","culprit":"Generic 'standing water' (and 'pipe') being mapped to Water Utility Problems without requiring utility-asset/leak evidence, ignoring street/drainage/development cues","fix":"Treat as Water Utility Problems only when a potable-water asset or active leak/break is named or clearly implied; otherwise, outdoor flooding/erosion/pipe work tied to rain, streets, grading/development, or drainage components belongs in Sidewalk Snow Removal."}

{"dimension":"traffic-safety sight distance vs private-property maintenance/encroachment","gt_signal":"driver visibility is impaired at an intersection/corner/driveway/curve (e.g., “can’t see to pull out,” “line of sight,” named road corners, Risk Management visibility report) with focus on motorists and roadway safety","pr_signal":"the issue is the condition or encroachment of vegetation/junk on a specific property (tall grass, weeds, yard/hedge overgrowth, sidewalk/yard impacts) without a motorist visibility context","culprit":"the Line of Sight negative rule that forces anything originating from a specific private property’s hedge/fence/yard—even at a corner—into Excessive Growth","fix":"Treat any vegetation that impairs motorists’ sight distance on public roads (intersections, corners, driveways, curves, medians) as Line of Sight regardless of property ownership, and reserve Excessive Growth for private overgrowth not affecting drivers’ visibility."}

{"dimension":"Source/ownership of the obstructing vegetation (private parcel vs public right‑of‑way/city‑maintained)","gt_signal":"Cues that the growth originates from a specific private property—mentions of a yard, hedge, fence line, driveway, corner lot/cul‑de‑sac—i.e., encroachment from a parcel onto the public way","pr_signal":"Vegetation clearly in the public right‑of‑way/median/city parcel or tied to roadway infrastructure (e.g., stop sign, arterial/avenue, traffic island) causing motorists’ visibility hazards, with no indicators it’s a private yard/hedge","culprit":"Intersection/visibility phrasing (\"intersection\", \"can’t see\", \"dangerous\") is over-weighted to Line of Sight, while the model ignores private-origin cues like \"yard/hedge/driveway/corner\" and seems to require a named address to treat it as private","fix":"Prioritize origin: treat reports implying a specific yard/hedge/driveway/corner lot as Excessive Growth even when they mention visibility at an intersection, and reserve Line of Sight for vegetation in the public right‑of‑way/medians/city property or tied to traffic control devices."}

{"dimension":"Intent and locus: a request for utility-side operational work on distribution hardware vs a customer tap-level condition/admin request","gt_signal":"Caller is asking the utility to dispatch a crew to operate/repair city assets (curb stop, meter set, main/hydrant)—e.g., turn water on/off (especially after-hours)—or reports persistent/widespread discoloration implying main/system flushing or repair beyond a single tap","pr_signal":"Report is limited to tap-level aesthetics (taste/odor/color), pressure/noise, or a check/inspection with no confirmed utility asset fault, framed as a premises/account issue rather than a field operation","culprit":"Water Quality positive rule allowing generic turn-on/turn-off/service activation and the broad discoloration-at-tap rule matched these items (on/off requests and multi-week brown water) despite signals of field ops/persistent system issue","fix":"Route any request that requires operating/repairing city-side hardware (including curb-stop turn-ons/offs and persistent system-wide discoloration) to Water Utility Problems, reserving Water Quality for tap-level taste/odor/pressure/noise and purely administrative activations without field work."}

{"dimension":"Intent and confirmation: customer-premises service/quality inquiry vs confirmed utility-asset failure requiring repair","gt_signal":"Single-premises symptom or account service (turn-on/off), or a suspected/unconfirmed leak needing inspection at/near the meter/premises with no mention of standing/gushing water, damage, or public-asset repair","pr_signal":"Explicit need to repair or secure a utility-owned asset (main, hydrant, curb stop, meter hardware), surfacing/standing water or confirmed break, contractor damage, or systemic dirty/sooty/gritty water requiring utility flushing","culprit":"Over-broad matching of keywords like “leak” and “meter pit” to the WUP rule about explicit leaks of meters/meter pits/lids, and “turn on” to curb-stop repair operations, ignoring lack of repair/confirmation context","fix":"Treat turn-on/off for account activation and vague/suspected leaks (even at the meter pit) with no surfacing water or asset damage as Water Quality, reserving Water Utility Problems for confirmed leaks/damage to utility assets, surfacing water, or systemic dirty/sooty water."}

{"dimension":"Which utility system the issue implicates: sanitary sewer/wastewater collection vs potable water distribution","gt_signal":"Explicit sewer context: sewer assets or functions are named (sewer main/lateral/manhole; sewer/lift/grinder/private ejector pumps), or sewer behaviors are described (clog/backup/slow drain, sewer/H2S odor), or the request ties inspection/flush/restoration explicitly to sewer mains/laterals—even if the text also says “water,” “leak,” or describes flow in the street","pr_signal":"Explicit potable-water distribution context: water mains/service lines, hydrants, meters/meter pits/lids, curb stops, suspected water-line leaks causing wet yards, or system-wide tap water quality issues; restoration only when tied to water-line work","culprit":"Overbroad keywording to Water Utility on generic tokens like “water/leak/running in street,” “yard repair,” and “lines,” so the Water Utility restoration/leak heuristics overrode clear sewer cues such as “sewer pump,” “clog/ran lines,” and “new sewer main”","fix":"Give precedence to sewer-specific assets/actions (sewer pump, sewer main/lateral/manhole, clog/backup/ran lines, sewer-tied restoration) and only classify as Water Utility when potable-water assets or tap-water symptoms are explicitly implicated."}

{"dimension":"Which material stream the note is evaluating (yard‑waste set‑out vs recycling set‑out), not which contaminant is named","gt_signal":"The subject is the yard‑waste stream: violations or prep instructions about brush/leaves set‑out (bundling, containers, weight/season/timing) or contamination of a yard‑waste pile/cart with non‑program items—even if those contaminants are recyclables like cardboard","pr_signal":"The subject is the recycling stream: issues about preparing or sorting recyclables, recycling cart/bin contamination, or bundling/flattening cardboard for recycling, typically keyed to a recycling container or explicit recycling prep context","culprit":"Over‑reliance on surface cues: Recycling pos rule (explicit 'recycling' + contamination) and Yard‑Waste neg rule (tie/bundle about cardboard -> Recycling)","fix":"Classify by the stream being inspected—keep contamination or prep notes with the yard‑waste set‑out in Yard Waste even if they mention recyclables/cardboard, and require a recycling‑container/context anchor to assign Recycling."}

{"dimension":"nature and origin of the obstruction: organic/yard-generated material from a property vs intentionally placed non‑organic equipment/containers in the public right‑of‑way","gt_signal":"vegetation or yard‑derived material (trees, limbs, logs, hedges, weeds) or property‑generated debris that encroaches/spills from a specific property onto a sidewalk/alley, even if it obstructs passage","pr_signal":"deliberately staged, non‑vegetative freestanding objects (dumpsters, trailers, pods, machinery, construction materials) occupying the street/sidewalk/right‑of‑way","culprit":"the over‑broad “freestanding object in the street/sidewalk → Blocked Street” rule (Excessive Growth neg) that treats yard waste/logs as generic objects","fix":"Explicitly route trees/limbs/logs and other yard‑waste or vegetation from a property—even when on the sidewalk/alley—to Excessive Growth, reserving Blocked Street for intentionally placed non‑vegetative containers/equipment/materials."}

{"dimension":"Effect on the public travelway vs. private property maintenance","gt_signal":"It describes vegetation intruding into the public right‑of‑way/roadway (“three feet into the right of way”), i.e., an obstruction that impedes passage in the street/sidewalk/alley regardless of the obstruction’s material.","pr_signal":"Mentions of grass/weeds/shrubbery tied to a specific property and framed as trimming/maintenance (“needs to be trimmed back,” lawn/lot conditions) without explicitly stating the public way is blocked.","culprit":"Blocked Street neg rule: “if bushes, weeds, or trees from a specific property encroach onto sidewalk or right‑of‑way, classify as Excessive Growth instead.”","fix":"Classify any obstruction that encroaches into and impedes movement in the public right‑of‑way as Blocked Street—even if caused by vegetation—reserving Excessive Growth for overgrowth that is a property‑maintenance issue not blocking travel."}

{"dimension":"Waste-stream specificity (which program/material the rule applies to) rather than the generic compliance action (sticker/size/weight/missed pickup).","gt_signal":"Any cue that the yard-waste program is the subject: explicit yard-waste/yardwaste/brush/leaves/branches terms, program code cues (e.g., 952), or the yard-waste–specific 40‑lb limit—even when the text is about stickers, 35‑gal cans, overweight, or a missed pickup.","pr_signal":"Compliance language with no stream cue—\"must have sticker,\" \"exceeds weight limit,\" \"can exceeds 35 gal,\" or \"missed pick-up\"—which is being defaulted to generic Trash.","culprit":"The Yard Waste negatives that shunt missed pickups and sticker/35‑gal mentions to Trash unless \"yard waste\" is spelled out, combined with treating the 40‑lb limit as a generic Trash trigger instead of a yard‑waste cue.","fix":"Prioritize the waste stream: if any yard‑waste indicator (yard‑waste terms, code 952, or the 40‑lb yard‑waste limit) appears, keep it in Yard Waste even for missed pickups or sticker/size/weight violations; otherwise treat generic compliance as Trash."}

{"dimension":"Responsibility/context: private‑property condition vs municipal trash collection/compliance","gt_signal":"Accumulation or overgrowth on private grounds (yard, back/side of house, porch, between houses, rear of property) with no curb/hauler/pickup/compliance context, even if described as 'trash', 'bags', or noting rodents","pr_signal":"Issues tied to the collection program or service points (stickers, can size, curb setout, missed/return pickup, crew handling, or overflowing carts/dumpsters placed for service)","culprit":"Excessive Growth neg rule that auto-routes any mention of household garbage/odor/rodents/dumpster to Trash, overriding private‑property context","fix":"Prefer private‑property context over waste keywords: classify as Excessive Growth whenever the mess is on a yard/porch/behind/side of a house without pickup/compliance/overflow cues, and reserve Trash for curbside/hauler or overflowing service-container issues."}

{"dimension":"Program/stream context (which waste stream the ticket is about) vs. generic service outcome/compliance (missed pickup, size/weight, stickers)","gt_signal":"It’s explicitly in the recycling stream (mentions recycle/recycling/blue cart/bin/toter or a missed recycling pickup), i.e., the problem is about the recycling program even if the issue is a miss, can size, weight, or a courtesy return","pr_signal":"Issue-type cues without stream gating: missed/partial pickup, courtesy return, overweight, oversize can—treated as Trash regardless of whether the stream is recycling","culprit":"Trash.pos rules for missed collection and set‑out violations are applied stream‑agnostically, and Recycling.neg wrongly forces any collection failure (even for recycling) into Trash","fix":"Gate on stream first: if the text indicates the recycling program/cart, classify under Recycling even when the complaint is a missed pickup or set‑out/weight/size violation; reserve Trash for cases with no recycling stream indicated."}

{"dimension":"Stream identity (what material/program the set‑out belongs to) vs generic compliance attributes (weight, can size, stickers/fees) that are shared across streams","gt_signal":"Only compliance cues are present (40‑lb/35‑gal limits, tags/stickers, per‑bag fee) with no content or program markers tying it to the yard‑waste stream; default to household trash compliance/enforcement","pr_signal":"An explicit yard‑waste stream anchor is present: yard waste/brush/leaves/branches/Christmas tree terms, seasonal timing like no winter collection, or clearly yard‑waste‑specific prep/fee language","culprit":"Yard Waste positive rule that treats “40‑lb limit” (with sticker/can‑size cues) as sufficient for Yard Waste even without any yard‑waste terms","fix":"Require an explicit yard‑waste stream reference (material or seasonal/program cue) to classify as Yard Waste; otherwise treat weight/size/sticker/fee compliance notes as Trash."}

{"dimension":"Material type/intent: sanitary removal of discarded waste vs. vegetation/property maintenance (growth)","gt_signal":"Mentions of discarded materials needing pickup—trash/garbage/litter/junk/debris, bags, dumped boards/items, or brush piled in the street/alley/yard—with a cleanup/removal intent (e.g., “scattered trash,” “trashed,” “bag in backyard”).","pr_signal":"Focus on plants being overgrown or needing cutting/trim—grass/weeds/shrubs/trees—without a discard/removal-of-waste problem; property-maintenance tone rather than sanitation.","culprit":"Trash.neg: \"if accumulation on private grounds (yard/behind/beside/lot) with no curbside/hauler/dumpster/cart context, classify as Excessive Growth instead\"","fix":"Classify by substance, not location: any discarded solid waste (trash/litter/junk, including brush piles) is Trash even on private property, while Excessive Growth is live/attached vegetation or pure mowing/trim issues; when both appear, prefer Trash."}

{"dimension":"Responsibility/context of the obstruction: public‑roadway sight‑distance hazard vs private‑property overgrowth/encroachment","gt_signal":"Mentions a specific property source (yard/hedge/fence/house/apartment), sidewalk encroachment forcing pedestrians into the street, or a driveway/frontage context without naming the public road being entered; sometimes just “overgrown/dangerous” corners with no explicit sight‑distance wording.","pr_signal":"Explicit motorist visibility on a public street: named intersections/roads with “can’t see traffic/vehicles” or “can’t see to pull out onto [road]”, reports from Risk Management/traffic safety, or vegetation clearly in ROW/medians/shoulders.","culprit":"LoS keywords like “can’t see”, “pulling out”, and “intersection” are being treated as sufficient triggers, overriding private‑property or sidewalk cues that should push the case to Excessive Growth.","fix":"Only classify as Line of Sight when the vegetation is in the public right‑of‑way or the text explicitly involves seeing traffic while entering/crossing a public roadway; if it originates from a specific private property or blocks sidewalks, it belongs in Excessive Growth even if visibility/safety is mentioned."}

{"dimension":"Origin and system responsible for the water (stormwater drainage/runoff vs pressurized potable water utility assets)","gt_signal":"References to stormwater context: rain/runoff, storm drains/inlets/catch basins/ditches/culverts/standpipes, street ponding/flooding, drainage from development/grading/parking-lot changes, or requests to install/adjust drainage components","pr_signal":"Explicit potable-water assets or symptoms: mains/service lines, meters/meter pits/lids, hydrants, curb-stops/shutoff valves, dirty/discolored water systemwide, or yard-only saturated spots suspected as underground service leaks with no drainage context","culprit":"'Standing water' being matched to the Water Utility Problems rule for yard leaks without enforcing the 'yard-only/private property' qualifier or excluding street/drainage/development cues","fix":"Classify by source/system: water tied to storm-drain features, street ponding, or development/grading (including requests for standpipes/inlets) is Sidewalk Snow Removal, while only explicit potable-asset failures or yard-only leak suspicions are Water Utility Problems."}

{"dimension":"Intent of the request: operational collection/crew action vs resident compliance/education about preparation","gt_signal":"Language about collection outcome or a service action is present (missed/not picked up/others collected but not here; return requested; crew went out/picked; deliver/replace cart) — i.e., the hauler is expected to act, even if the material is ‘recycling’.","pr_signal":"Only sorting/contamination/preparation issues are noted (not properly sorted, trash mixed in, non-recyclables, instruction like “must be sorted”), with no pickup failure, return request, or crew/hauler action implied.","culprit":"Recycling positive rule: explicit recycling cue + unsorted/contamination is over-broad and fires even when collection failure/crew-action cues are present.","fix":"Prioritize service intent: if the text asks for or reports a pickup/return or other hauler action, classify as Trash even when recycling/contamination is mentioned; reserve Recycling for education/violation about sorting/preparation without a pickup request."}

{"dimension":"Source/responsibility of the obstruction: private-property growth/junk encroaching vs freestanding objects placed in the public right‑of‑way","gt_signal":"Overgrowth, detached limbs/logs/yard waste, or household junk tied to a specific property (porch/yard/lot) even if it spills onto a sidewalk/alley, or hazards not about passing in the ROW","pr_signal":"Dumpsters, roll‑offs, trailers or other placed/staged objects sitting in the street/alley/sidewalk and narrowing or blocking passage","culprit":"Blocked Street positive rule 'Physical obstruction that blocks a public travelway' is too broad and overrode the yard‑waste/private‑origin cues (e.g., logs in sidewalk, overgrown weeds/limbs)","fix":"Treat obstructions made of private-property growth, detached yard waste, or property clutter as Excessive Growth, reserving Blocked Street for freestanding placed items occupying the right‑of‑way."}

{"dimension":"Which material stream the note is evaluating (yard‑waste set‑out vs recycling set‑out), not which contaminant is named","gt_signal":"The subject is the yard‑waste stream: violations or prep instructions about brush/leaves set‑out (bundling, containers, weight/season/timing) or contamination of a yard‑waste pile/cart with non‑program items—even if those contaminants are recyclables like cardboard","pr_signal":"The subject is the recycling stream: issues about preparing or sorting recyclables, recycling cart/bin contamination, or bundling/flattening cardboard for recycling, typically keyed to a recycling container or explicit recycling prep context","culprit":"Over‑reliance on surface cues: Recycling pos rule (explicit 'recycling' + contamination) and Yard‑Waste neg rule (tie/bundle about cardboard -> Recycling)","fix":"Classify by the stream being inspected—keep contamination or prep notes with the yard‑waste set‑out in Yard Waste even if they mention recyclables/cardboard, and require a recycling‑container/context anchor to assign Recycling."}

{"dimension":"Cause/responsibility: utility-restoration of disturbed surfaces vs routine private yard vegetation maintenance","gt_signal":"Mentions of yard/driveway repair or restoration (e.g., drive repair, yard repair/reseed, backfill/settlement, restoration after digging/meter/line work) indicating the water utility disturbed and must restore the surface","pr_signal":"Explicit vegetation maintenance cues (grass/weeds/shrubs overgrown, mowing/cutting needed, weed height, vacant lot overgrowth) with no link to utility work or surface restoration","culprit":"Over-broad match on the word “yard/yard work” to Excessive Growth’s private overgrowth rule, while missing restoration/drive-repair cues","fix":"Differentiate generic “yard/drive repair/restoration” requests tied to utility work from vegetation overgrowth, and require explicit growth/mowing/weed terms to trigger Excessive Growth."}

{"dimension":"Operational responsibility and scope: public-side distribution/field operations vs customer-premises symptoms or account service","gt_signal":"Signals that a utility crew must work on public assets or a system condition exists beyond a single tap—e.g., curb-stop/meter/main operations tied to repairs, confirmed leaks/standing water, or persistent multi-day discoloration affecting the residence/area","pr_signal":"Symptoms confined to a customer tap or an administrative request without evidence of a public-side fault—e.g., taste/odor/color/pressure/noise at one premises or start/stop/turn-on for account activation","culprit":"Overbroad Water Quality positives: (1) 'Turn-on/turn-off requests...' (treats repair-related curb-stop ops as account service), and (2) generic 'discoloration at a customer tap' (reinforced by WUP neg on color at taps) that ignores persistence","fix":"Differentiate intent and scope: only treat turn-on/turn-off as Water Quality when it explicitly refers to account activation/deactivation, while persistent multi-day discoloration indicating a distribution-system condition should go to Water Utility Problems"}

{"dimension":"confirmation/stage of incident: unconfirmed symptom/inspection request vs confirmed public-asset failure needing repair","gt_signal":"Reports that suggest or suspect a leak/issue at a specific premises or meter without visible water, damage, or an explicitly broken utility asset—i.e., language implying “check/inspect,” ambiguous location (“in front”), single-site context, and no standing water.","pr_signal":"Explicit, visible failures of utility infrastructure or aftermath: stated main breaks, broken/damaged valves or meter equipment, confirmed leaks at public assets, water surfacing/standing, contractor damage, or restoration needs.","culprit":"Over-broad matching to the Water Utility Problems rule “Explicit failures or leaks of public water distribution assets: mains/service lines, hydrants, curb stop/shutoff valves, or meters/meter pits/lids,” triggered by the keywords “leak” and “meter pit.”","fix":"Require explicit confirmation/visibility of a utility asset failure (e.g., broken, gushing, standing water) for Water Utility Problems; otherwise, treat unqualified or suspected leaks at/near a meter/main as Water Quality (inspection)."}

{"dimension":"Infrastructure/flow origin: sanitary sewer (wastewater) vs potable water distribution","gt_signal":"Mentions of sewer-specific assets or effects (sewer/sewage, laterals/mains/manholes, sewer/lift/grinder/private ejector pumps, H2S/sewer odor, backups/overflows/slow drains) or restoration explicitly tied to sewer work","pr_signal":"Mentions of potable water distribution assets or system-wide drinking-water issues (water mains/service lines, meters/meter pits/lids, hydrants, curb-stops/shutoff valves), unexplained wet ground suspected from water-line leaks, or restoration tied to water-utility work","culprit":"Over-broad Water Utility 'restoration after utility excavations' rule captured a request explicitly about a sewer main, and the model overweighted the word 'water' in 'sewer pump leaking water' instead of the sewer asset","fix":"Gate restoration and leak/runoff cues by named utility: only treat as Water Utility when a drinking-water asset or potable-water symptom is present; if a sewer asset/term (sewer main/lateral/manhole/pump) or wastewater discharge/odor is present, route to Sewer Problems."}

{"dimension":"Impact on public travelway passability vs. private-property upkeep","gt_signal":"Any vegetation or object occupying the physical space of a public right‑of‑way (street/sidewalk/alley/bike lane)—evidenced by terms like “into the right‑of‑way,” feet of intrusion, or block‑level encroachment—indicating passage is impeded even if “blocked/can’t pass” isn’t explicitly stated.","pr_signal":"Overgrowth described as a property maintenance issue (tall grass/weeds/hedges on a specific yard/lot) without a clear claim that the public travelway itself is being occupied or impassable, even if it brushes or lightly encroaches.","culprit":"Blocked Street NEG rule requiring explicit “blocked passage” phrasing; it overrode clear right‑of‑way encroachment cues like “three feet into the right of way.”","fix":"Key on encroachment into the public right‑of‑way itself (e.g., ‘into ROW,’ measured feet, sidewalk/street space taken) as Blocked Street even without explicit “cannot pass” language."}

{"pos":["Vegetation in a public right-of-way obstructs a driver's view of oncoming traffic or traffic-control devices on a public street","Vegetation limits motorists’ ability to see cross-traffic at a public intersection, corner, or roundabout","Vegetation prevents drivers from seeing to exit a driveway or alley onto a named public street","Vegetation in a median, island, shoulder, or ditch creates a sight-distance hazard for roadway users","A traffic-safety or Risk Management report identifies a vegetation-related sight-distance hazard on a public roadway"],"remap":["if vegetation originates from a specific private property’s yard, hedge, fence, or lot, classify as Excessive Growth instead","if the issue is vegetation encroaching on sidewalks/paths or forcing pedestrians into the street, classify as Excessive Growth instead","if a driveway/frontage/parking-lot visibility complaint omits the name of the public street being entered, classify as Excessive Growth instead","if an intersection report lacks explicit driver-action phrasing (e.g., pull out, turn, merge, approach) or public right-of-way location, classify as Excessive Growth instead"]}

{"pos":["Reports of clogged or blocked storm drains, inlets, catch basins, driveway culverts, ditches, or standpipes.","Storm sewer backing up, surcharging, or not conveying runoff during or after rain.","Standing or ponded water on streets or public right-of-way due to rainfall or blocked inlets.","Requests to install, adjust, or maintain public drainage components (inlets, culverts, standpipes, pipes, outfalls).","Drainage complaints or questions tied to grading, development, or parking-lot changes affecting runoff."],"remap":["if mentions water mains/service lines, meters, valves, hydrants, or shutoffs, classify as Water Utility Problems instead.","if yard-only standing water, no rain/storm/drain terms, and suspected leak, classify as Water Utility Problems instead.","if sanitary sewer backups, manholes overflowing, or sewage odors, classify as Sewer Problems instead.","if snow or ice on sidewalks or failure to shovel sidewalks, classify as Street Snow Removal instead."]}
